verdict.rationale: Mailchimp documents outbound HTTP POST webhooks in both products. Transactional webhooks cover message events (send, bounce, open, click, and others). Marketing audience webhooks deliver subscription, email-change and campaign-sending updates to a user-supplied URL, with documented signature verification and test/debug guidance. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, explicit evidence of programmatic (API-based) webhook registration, and freedom from plan gating (webhooks need the Standard or Premium plan).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: There are three types of webhooks that Mailchimp Transactional currently POSTs: **Message events**: send, deferral, hard-bounce, soft-bounce, delivered, open, click, spam, unsub, reject
By entering a valid URL that’s set up to accept HTTP POST requests, you can receive updates on subscriptions, changed email addresses, campaign sending, and more.
Webhooks allow your application to receive information about email events as they occur and respond in a way that you define.
